issues.description: play.ts is a developer scratchpad and should not be in the patch
issues.detail: The diff swaps the canonical `zod/v4` import for a relative path into `packages/zod/src/index.js` and dumps console.log debugging. This is a maintainer's local scribble, not a change to ship. Drop play.ts from the PR or revert it. THREE-PATCHES: the scratchpad is not part of the feature.

issues.description: Quadratic JSON.stringify dedup inside a nested key loop is the wrong shape
issues.detail: finalize() now walks `for (const key in schema)` and calls `JSON.stringify(schema[key]) === JSON.stringify(refSeen.def![key])` on every key, in two separate places, for every seen schema. On large schemas with nested objects this is O(N*size) at minimum and pathological for deep trees. Compare by reference where possible, or compute the def fingerprint once. BAD-TASTE.

issues.description: Override semantics silently changed; overrideCount jumped 6 to 12 with no explanation
issues.detail: The old code guarded `if (!seen.isParent) ctx.override(...)`. The new code unconditionally calls override. The test was updated from 6 to 12 to make it pass, but the test's name is `do not run on references` — doubling the call count is exactly running on references. Either the test name is now a lie or the behavior regressed. Explain which, in the commit message, before this lands.

issues.description: Commit does at least three things; should be three patches
issues.detail: This diff (a) reworks parent/ref tracking in process/finalize, (b) changes fileProcessor output shape (anyOf hoisting shared props to root — a user-visible JSON Schema change), and (c) flips the mini ZodType to pass `{parent: true}`. Each is independently reviewable and independently revertable. THREE-PATCHES.

issues.description: Recursive flattenRef on seen.parent can re-enter and is fragile
issues.detail: flattenRef now calls `flattenRef(seen.parent)` after already running for `ref`, relying on `seen.ref === null` as the recursion guard. But `seen.parent` is a different field with no equivalent guard; if parent chains form a cycle (which they shouldn't, but the type system doesn't enforce it) you get a stack overflow. Add an explicit visited check or document the invariant.

issues.description: Dead commented-out line left in mini/schemas.ts neighborhood
issues.detail: The mini change just uncomments `{ parent: true }` that was previously commented out. Fine, but the surrounding code and the classic counterpart now diverge in subtle ways (classic passes `{parent: true}` from check(), mini does the same in ZodMiniType). Worth a one-line comment in the commit message saying these are now intentionally symmetric, so the next maintainer doesn't re-diverge them by accident.

review.summary: NEEDS-WORK. The core idea — tracking `parent` separately from processor-set `ref` so $ref propagation survives wrappers like `readonly().meta({id}).describe()` — is reasonable and the new test case demonstrates a real fix. But the patch is the wrong shape to land: it bundles three independent changes (parent/ref rework, fileProcessor anyOf hoisting, mini parent flag), ships a debugging scratchpad in play.ts, silently doubles override invocations against a test literally named "do not run on references", and introduces JSON.stringify-based dedup loops that will bite on large schemas. Split into three patches, drop play.ts, justify or revert the override-count change, and replace the stringify dedup with structural comparison. Then it can land.
